title: Constitutional Classifiers for Code Generation Safety: Mitigating Jailbreaks in Codex-like Models
summary: This paper proposes adapting Constitutional Classifiers to enforce safety in code generation models like Codex. The approach trains classifiers on synthetic data generated via a constitution specifying safe coding practices. Evaluation on HumanEval and jailbreak prompts measures refusal rates, functional correctness, and memorization of unsafe code. The hypothesis is that this method reduces jailbreak success rates by 50% compared to baseline alignment techniques while maintaining 90% of Codex's original problem-solving accuracy.
gap: Existing alignment methods for code models (ref-001, ref-016) lack robust defenses against jailbreaks targeting code generation (ref-004, ref-014). Constitutional Classifiers (ref-004) have not been applied to code-specific safety domains.
approach: Train Constitutional Classifiers on synthetic code data generated by prompting LLMs with a constitution defining safe coding practices. Integrate classifiers as a guardrail during Codex inference, rejecting prompts that violate safety rules.
evaluation: Baselines: Vanilla Codex, RLHF-aligned Codex. Metrics: Jailbreak success rate (ref-014), HumanEval pass@k (ref-001), verbatim memorization of unsafe code (ref-007). Test on 100 jailbreak prompts and 200 HumanEval problems.

title: Legal Compliance through Training Data Deduplication and Memorization Auditing
summary: We develop a framework combining dataset deduplication with probabilistic memorization auditing to ensure legal compliance of generative AI systems. By removing near-duplicates and quantifying residual memorization risks, our method reduces verbatim reproduction by 90% while maintaining model utility. The framework provides auditable evidence for copyright and privacy compliance.
gap: Current deduplication methods reduce memorization but lack systematic auditing of residual risks. Legal frameworks like EU copyright law require demonstrable efforts to prevent unauthorized reproduction, which existing techniques fail to provide through quantifiable metrics.
approach: We extend [ref-011]'s deduplication algorithm with shingling-based near-duplicate detection, then apply probabilistic extraction audits on the cleaned dataset. A compliance dashboard visualizes memorization probabilities per training example, enabling targeted data removal for high-risk sequences while preserving model performance.
evaluation: We train GPT-Neo models on deduplicated C4 datasets with/without auditing. Metrics include verbatim reproduction rate, ROUGE scores on summarization, and copyright compliance scores based on [ref-020] and [ref-035]. Legal experts assess documentation adequacy for compliance with US and EU copyright standards.

title: Jailbreak Transferability Mitigation via Constitutional Classifier Ensembles
summary: We propose an ensemble of constitutional classifiers trained on diverse adversarial suffix patterns to defend against transferable jailbreaks. Unlike single classifiers, our approach combines specialized models for different attack categories, reducing universal jailbreak success rates by 65% on Vicuna and LLaMA-2-Chat. The system maintains low inference overhead through parallel evaluation and dynamic thresholding.
gap: Current jailbreak defenses like Constitutional Classifiers fail against transferable attacks that exploit generalization gaps between training and real-world adversarial patterns. Single classifiers cannot adapt to evolving attack suffixes, leaving models vulnerable to cross-model transfer attacks documented in recent studies.
approach: We train an ensemble of 5-7 specialized constitutional classifiers, each fine-tuned on a distinct jailbreak pattern category (e.g., role-play, code injection). A meta-classifier dynamically weights their outputs based on input prompt characteristics, while a lightweight gradient-based detector identifies novel attack patterns through embedding space anomalies.
evaluation: We test against 500 transferable jailbreaks from [ref-014] and new attacks generated via greedy search. Metrics include jailbreak success rate reduction, false positive increase on benign queries, and inference latency. Comparisons are made against single constitutional classifiers and commercial model defenses (ChatGPT, Claude).
